population.condition: Bile acid diarrhea (BAD), idiopathic or postcholecystectomy, SeHCAT-verified moderate-to-severe
key_inclusion_criteria: Idiopathic or postcholecystectomy bile acid diarrhea
evidence: The study included 52 patients with moderate-to-severe, SeHCAT-verified bile acid diarrhea. The article reports mean ages separately by treatment group, but not an overall mean age. fileciteturn22file0

Key eligibility criteria included a SeHCAT result ≤10%, no diabetes, and no other gastrointestinal diseases. The reported sex counts (32 women and 18 men) do not sum to the stated total of 52; therefore, the overall female percentage is not recorded. fileciteturn22file0

arms.name: Liraglutide
arms.dose: 0.6 mg daily, uptitrated by weekly increments of 0.6 mg to 1.8 mg daily over 3 weeks
evidence: Participants were randomized to 6 weeks of liraglutide treatment, starting at 0.6 mg daily and increasing by 0.6 mg weekly to 1.8 mg daily over 3 weeks. One participant withdrew because of gastrointestinal side effects. fileciteturn22file0

arms.name: Colesevelam
evidence: Participants were randomized to 6 weeks of oral colesevelam treatment at 1,875 mg twice daily. One participant withdrew because of gastrointestinal side effects. fileciteturn22file0
